newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Higher air freight halts Bangladesh produce exports.
newsitem.headline: Higher air freight halts Bangladesh produce exports.

text.p: Bangladeshi traders have stopped exporting fruits and vegetables by national airline Biman after it imposed higher air freight from March 1.

"We have stopped exporting our products by Biman in protest against increase of air freight," Farid Uddin Ahmed, president of the Bangladesh Fruits, Vegetables and Allied Products Exporters Association, said on Monday.
"We suffered at least $3 million in lost export earnings over the past two weeks," he told Reuters.
He said Biman raised cargo freight by 15 percent.

One Biman official said on Monday a 20 percent increase in jet fuel prices on the international market and repeated downward adjustment of the Bangladesh currency taka against the U.S. dollar had forced it to raise freight charges.
"It's still lower compared to the fuel price hike," he said, adding that Biman had not increased passenger fares.
Ahmed said Bangladesh would not be able to compete with other exporters of fruits and vegetables. India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Cyprus and Kenya are Bangladesh's main competitors.
Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, and a number of European countries buy fruits and vegetables from Bangladesh.
